applied.problem: "A power belongs only to the number it touches" is false of (−3)², where the square touches the bracket, so the rule as stated contradicts its own example; "power" and "BIDMAS" are also used without ever saying what they are.

"Only (−3)² = 9" is false as an "only" claim (3² = 9 too); the rule of thumb has the same number-versus-bracket slip as the explanation; and BIDMAS, read alone in the dossier, is never said to be the order's memory word.

notes.problem: −3² = −9 is the standard maths convention, but some spreadsheets (Excel reads =-3^2 as 9) apply the minus before the power; worth a line in lesson 9, where Dan keys negatives into tools, since the brackets advice here already protects him.
